title: Many timers
description:
Model `SetTimer`: several timers with ids and intervals, each sending `WM_TIMER` when due.

```
timer 1 every 100 ms, timer 2 every 250 ms
t=100 WM_TIMER 1
t=200 WM_TIMER 1
t=250 WM_TIMER 2
t=300 WM_TIMER 1
KillTimer(1) -> only timer 2 from now on
```
hints: For each timer with `due <= now`, add it to the list and set `due = now + interval` (lesson 2.03).
Sort the result by the due time before rescheduling so the order is right.
requirements: `setTimer(id, ms)` replaces a timer with the same id; `killTimer(id)` stops it.
`advance(now)` returns the timer messages due, in time order.
A slow frame does not make a timer fire many times in a row: like Windows, it fires once and is rescheduled.
stretch: Compare with a game loop clock using `QueryPerformanceCounter`, which does not drift.
